newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: Czech C.Bank says crown rate "more realistic".
newsitem.headline: Czech C.Bank says crown rate "more realistic".

text.p: The current rate of the Czech crown against its mark/dollar basket is "more realistic" than the levels seen in February, Czech National Bank spokesman Martin Svehla told Reuters on Friday.
"This level which the crown holds now is more adequate I would say, " said Svehla. "In comparison to the previous situation this is better..or this is more realistic," he said.
The crown was fixed at a record high of plus 5.51 percent against the mid-point of the basket in early February but was trading at plus 1.25 percent from the mid-point on Friday morning.
The crown appreciated sharply in January and February pushed by the issue of more than 40 billion crowns of crown-denominated Eurobonds.
But after the central bank described the Eurobond wave as irrational and the crown's then level as unrealistic, the Czech currency fell back sharply.
Before Svehla's comments, dealers said on Friday morning that sentiment was still bearish about the crown and that the currency had been under strong selling pressure, especially from London.
